requirements.requirement: The system shall record an audit entry for every sensitive change.

In Milestone 1 the following shall be audited: users (create, role change, activation), role permissions, all admin settings lists, company responsible-salesperson changes and deletions, contract status and commercial terms, contract payments.
The audit mechanism shall be generic so that Milestone 2 and 3 entities (pricing rules, discounts, discount approvals, deals, payments) are added without changing the audit design.
Audit entries shall be written in the same database transaction as the change, so a change is never saved without its audit entry.
Audit entries shall be append-only: no user, including the Administrator, can edit or delete them through the application.
Users with "Audit log: view" shall see the audit log in the admin panel with filters by date range, user, entity type and action, and can open an entry to see the old/new values side by side.
Secrets (passwords, tokens) shall never be stored in audit entries; such fields are shown as "changed".
The audit log shall be exportable to CSV for the filtered range.

The platform shall display the Wellness Plus – Better Living logo (provided in "revizedtWELLNESS PLUS.docx", reproduced in section 3.1) in the login page, application header, browser tab (favicon, using the leaf-and-cross symbol) and emails sent by the system.
The platform shall use the Wellness Albania colour palette and fonts from the branding guidelines, applied through the design tokens in tokens.css (light and dark mode).
The login, forgot-password and reset-password pages shall be redesigned with Wellness Albania branding (logo, colours, background image if provided).
The product name shall read "Wellness Albania" in page titles, header and system emails.
Self-service tenant sign-up, subscription and SaaS marketing screens inherited from the SaaS CRM shall be hidden or disabled.
Authorised users shall create and edit companies with the fields in the table above, with validation messages in the user's language.
When the user selects the business type, the system shall set the risk level automatically from the business type configuration.
The location shall be captured as Area and City chosen from predefined lists, plus an optional free-text street address.
A company shall have one or more contact persons, each with name, position/title, phone and email.
The company page shall show the complete history in one timeline: contacts added, notes, activities (calls, emails, visits, meetings), offers, deals and contracts, newest first, filterable by type.
The company list shall support search by name, contact name, phone and email, and filters by business type, risk level, area, city, salesperson and status.
If the configured risk level of a business type changes, companies of that type shall show the new risk level.
Existing client data shall be migrated: legacy fields and relevant custom field values map to the new columns; unmapped values stay visible as custom fields.
Deleting a company shall be a soft delete (existing deletedAt), restricted per section 4.2, and written to the audit log.
Albanian (sq) shall be the default language; English (en) shall be the second main language.
Every new screen, message, validation error and email introduced in Milestone 1 shall be translated in sq and en.
Lookup values managed by the Administrator (business types, risk levels, areas, cities, reasons, statuses) shall have an Albanian and an English label.
Dates, numbers and currency shall follow the workspace locale (default: Albania, EUR/ALL as configured).
The system shall support the roles Sales User, Sales Manager, Reception / Operational Staff, Administrator and CEO, seeded with the default permissions in section 4.2.
A role shall be a set of permissions.
The Administrator shall edit, from the admin panel, which permissions each role has and, where applicable, its data scope (Own / Team / All).
The Administrator shall be able to create additional custom roles by copying an existing role.
Every API endpoint shall check the required permission and data scope on the server.
Fields a role may not see (e.g.
The menu, pages and actions shown in the frontend shall be derived from the user's permissions.
The system shall prevent removing the last user with "Manage roles & permissions" (lock-out protection).
Global visibility ("view all data") and system configuration ("manage settings") shall be separate permissions.
Every change to role permissions shall be written to the audit log, listing the permissions added and removed.
"Own" scope shall mean companies where the user is the responsible salesperson, and the activities, contacts, notes and (later) offers, deals and contracts of those companies.
"Team" scope shall mean all records of users holding the Sales User role, plus unassigned companies.
Search results, lists, counts and exports shall respect the data scope.
A new company created by a Sales User shall be assigned to that user by default.
The Administrator shall manage Business types, each linked to exactly one risk level (e.g.
The Administrator shall manage Risk levels (name/level number, description, order).
The Administrator shall manage the predefined list of Areas (e.g.
The Administrator shall manage the predefined list of Cities, each belonging to one Area.
The Administrator shall manage Follow-up intervals in days (default 3, 5, 7).
The Administrator shall manage the Lost-deal reasons (e.g.
The Administrator shall manage the labels, order and colour of Contract statuses: Draft, Pending Signature, Active, Expired, Suspended, Cancelled.
The Administrator shall manage the labels, order and colour of Payment statuses: Not Invoiced, Invoice Issued, Payment Pending, Partially Paid, Paid, Overdue (fixed set, as FR-SET-07).
The Administrator shall edit general workspace settings: company name, default language, time zone, date format, currency.
Seed data shall provide placeholder values for all lists, to be replaced by Wellness Albania's real lists (section 8).
Users shall log in with email and password.
The Administrator shall create users (name, email, phone, language, role) and the system shall send an invitation email to set a password.
Each user shall have exactly one role.
The Administrator shall deactivate and reactivate users.
Before a Sales User with assigned companies is deactivated, the system shall ask the Administrator or Sales Manager to reassign those companies to another Sales User.
Role changes, activation/deactivation and user creation shall be written to the audit log (section 6).
No hard-coded user-facing text; all strings through i18next.
Code follows .agentrules (Clean Architecture, TDD).
Database migrations shall be reversible or backed up, and run on both PostgreSQL and MySQL targets.
Company list and search shall return in under 1 second for 10,000 companies; permission checks add no noticeable delay.
Permissions and data scope shall be enforced in the application layer for every request; repositories keep structural tenant isolation.
Passwords hashed with bcrypt; sessions via the existing JWT mechanism; all traffic over HTTPS.
Personal data (contact persons) shall be processed in line with GDPR and the Albanian data protection law; data is stored in the EU.
All Milestone 1 screens shall work on desktop and mobile (from 360 px wide).

The platform shall calculate the monthly list price with the rules in section 4.1 and the current pricing configuration. If no employee band covers the number of employees, or the city belongs to no price zone, the platform shall show "Price on request" and not calculate a price.
Each component shall be rounded to the cent (half up) and the monthly list price is the sum of the rounded components, so the breakdown always adds up to the total.

For "Price on request" cases, a user with "Discounts: approve" (Sales Manager) may enter a manual monthly price with a reason. A Sales User may propose one, and it then needs Sales Manager approval like a discount above the cap (section 5).
The pricing screen shall show the price per employee and the annual value (monthly net price × contract months, default 12, FR-PCF-08) for information.
The price calculation shall reproduce every value of the proposed pricing model (Figure 1) and both worked examples in 4.1 to the cent.
Money shall be stored and calculated as Decimal (two decimals, half-up rounding), never as Float.

The permission catalogue shall add: Sales script: view / edit; Deals: view, create / edit (scoped Own/Team/All), reopen, delete; Offers: create / edit (scoped); Discounts: approve (scoped); Follow-ups: manage (scoped); Activity results: manage. The Administrator can assign them from the M1 roles screen.
The default roles shall receive the permissions in the matrix in 9.2 on upgrade, without changing permissions the Administrator already customised for Milestone 1.

Deals, offers, discounts, pricing and follow-up amounts shall be removed from API responses for users without "Commercial details: view" (extends M1 FR-RBAC-06). Deal and offer items are hidden from the company history for them.
The audit log viewer shall offer filters for the new entity types (Pricing, Offer, Deal, Discount approval, Sales script).
The discount cap, approval state, stage rules and data scope shall be enforced on the server for every request.
Rich text from the sales script and offer texts shall be sanitized on the server before storing and before rendering.

The Administrator shall manage employee bands: from and to number of employees, base fee for the first employee of the band's formula, and fee per extra employee. Bands cannot overlap. Seed: 1–10 employees, €30.00, €8.00.
The Administrator shall set a risk surcharge % for each risk level from Milestone 1. Seed: Level 1 (Low) 0%, Level 2 (Medium) 10%, Level 3 (High) 20% (Q4).
Percentages shall accept values from 0 to 1000 with up to two decimals; fees accept values ≥ 0 with two decimals.

The Administrator shall manage visit frequencies: label, visits per year (optional, for reports), and pricing type — percentage of base fee, or fixed monthly amount. Seed: 1/year 0%, 2/year 20%, 4/year 35%, 6/year 50%, Monthly 100%, Ad hoc fixed €15.00.

The Administrator shall manage price zones: label, surcharge %, and the list of predefined cities in the zone (picked from the M1 City list). A city may be in more than one zone (FR-PRC-06). The admin screen lists active cities that are in no zone.
The Administrator shall manage services (label and description, sq/en) and service packages (label, description, list of services, default package).
The Administrator shall set the discount cap: the highest discount % a salesperson may apply without approval (section 5).

The Administrator shall set offer settings: validity in days (default 30), default contract length in months (default 12), number prefix, Wellness Albania company details printed on the offer (name, NIPT, address, phone, email, website, bank details) and the standard offer texts (introduction, terms, closing) in sq and en.
The Administrator shall be able to try the current configuration in a test calculator on the settings page without creating an offer.

In Milestone 2 the following shall be audited with old and new values (using the M1 audit mechanism, FR-AUD-03): all pricing configuration (bands, risk surcharges, visit frequencies, price zones and their cities, discount cap, offer settings), services and packages, activity results, stage labels, sales script publishes, discount requests and decisions, offer status changes with prices, deal won / lost / reopen / delete, and changes of deal salesperson or agreed values.
A "Sales script" button shall be available to users with "Sales script: view" in the application header and on the company, deal and pricing screens.

The script shall open as a side panel on desktop and stay open while the user navigates between pages and fills in forms, until the user closes it. On a phone it opens full screen with a close button.

There shall be one script for all salespeople. It is organised in sections with headings and bullet points (e.g. Opening, Needs discovery, Pricing questions, Objections, Closing), and the panel shows the section headings as a clickable list.

Users with "Sales script: edit" (Administrator) shall edit the script in a rich-text editor (headings, bullets, numbered lists, bold, italic, links) in Albanian and in English, preview it, and publish it. Salespeople see the published version in their language; if the English text is empty they see the Albanian text.
Each publish shall be kept as a version with author and date, and written to the audit log. The Administrator can view earlier versions.
The Administrator shall be able to restore an earlier version as a new draft.
Salespeople can only read the script. There is no text-to-speech and no per-salesperson script.
The user can search the text of the script inside the panel.
All Milestone 2 screens, including the board, calendar, pricing screen and script panel, shall work on desktop and mobile from 360 px wide.

A user with "Deals: create / edit" shall create a deal for a company with: type (New contract, Renewal, Extra services), title (default "<company> – <type>"), responsible salesperson (default: the company's), expected close date (optional) and notes. A company can have several deals, open or closed.
Creating a company shall offer to create its first deal in stage New Lead at the same time.

The deal page shall show: company, contact persons, stage, value (net monthly and annual from the latest offer), offers with their versions and statuses, activities and follow-ups for this deal, stage history and notes. The sales script button is available on it.
Deals follow the data scope of Milestone 1: Own for Sales User, Team for Sales Manager, All for Administrator and CEO. Reception has no access to deals.
Changing the responsible salesperson of a deal requires "Companies: reassign" and is audited.

The pipeline stages shall be New Lead, Contacted, Interested, Offer Prepared, Offer Sent, Follow-Up, Negotiation, Won and Lost. The set is fixed in code (the platform logic depends on Won and Lost); the Administrator can change labels, order and colour, as for contract statuses in M1 FR-SET-07.
The salesperson shall move an open deal to any other open stage, forwards or backwards (Q10). Won and Lost are reached only through the win and lose actions (7.3).

The platform shall move a deal forward automatically: creating its first offer → Offer Prepared; marking an offer as sent → Offer Sent; scheduling a follow-up when the deal is in Offer Sent → Follow-Up; logging the first activity on a New Lead → Contacted. It never moves a deal backwards automatically.
Every stage change shall be recorded in the stage history: from, to, user (or "automatic"), date and time. The time spent in each stage and from creation to close is kept for Milestone 3 reports.

The pipeline shall be shown as a board with one column per open stage (and Won / Lost this month), cards showing company, deal title, net monthly value, salesperson and next follow-up date. Cards can be dragged between columns. Each column shows the number of deals and their total value.
The pipeline shall also be shown as a list with sorting and filters by salesperson, stage, deal type, business type, area, city, expected close date and value.
On a phone the board scrolls horizontally inside the board area and cards can be moved with a "Move to stage" action instead of dragging.
A deal can be deleted (soft delete) only by a user with "Deals: delete" and only if it has no offer marked as sent.
Deals and their stage changes shall appear in the company history timeline (M1 FR-CMP-05).
The pipeline board and calendar shall load in under 2 seconds with 2,000 open deals and 5,000 follow-ups.
The user shall record an activity of type Call, Email, Visit, Meeting, Online meeting or Note on a company, and optionally link it to one of the company's open deals.

An activity (other than Note) shall record: date and time it happened (default now, can be in the past), contact person (from the company's contacts), result (from a predefined list), client feedback (text), next action (text) and notes. The user who recorded it is stored automatically.
The Administrator shall manage the list of activity results (sq/en, order, active), e.g. Reached – interested, Reached – not interested, Not reached, Call back later, Meeting agreed, Offer requested.
Activities shall appear in the company history and on the linked deal, newest first, with type, date, user, contact person, result and next action.
The user who recorded an activity can edit it for 24 hours; after that only the Sales Manager can edit it. Activities are never deleted by Sales Users.
Existing Interactions shall be kept and shown as activities: MEETING, CALL, EMAIL and NOTE map to the new types, their date is the creation date, and the missing fields are left empty.
Migrations shall run on PostgreSQL and MySQL, including the migration of existing interactions (FR-ACT-07) and quotation references (FR-OFR-08), and be reversible or backed up.

A salesperson shall open the pricing screen from a company or a deal. The screen shows the four inputs, the calculated breakdown and the monthly price, and recalculates on the server whenever an input changes.

Inputs shall be pre-filled from the company record: number of employees, business type (and its risk level) and City. Location is never typed: it is the company's predefined City (Dimitris's comment). If the company has no City or business type, the screen asks the user to complete the company record and links to it.
The risk level shall follow the business type (M1 FR-CMP-02) and cannot be chosen directly on the pricing screen. Changing the business type on the pricing screen changes the risk surcharge.

The number of employees defaults to the company value and can be changed for this offer (whole number ≥ 1). Changing it on the pricing screen does not change the company record unless the user chooses "also update the company".
The visit frequency shall be chosen from the active visit frequencies (FR-PCF-04).

When a city belongs to more than one price zone (e.g. Tiranë: centre or suburbs), the salesperson shall choose the zone from those linked to the city. When it belongs to exactly one, the zone is set automatically.
The salesperson shall choose a service package (FR-PCF-06) on the pricing screen; the package describes the services in the offer. In this milestone the package does not change the price (Q11).
Saving the pricing screen creates or updates a draft offer for the deal (section 6). A price can also be calculated without saving, e.g. during a call.
A change to any pricing setting shall not change offers already created: each offer stores the inputs and the rule values it was calculated with (FR-OFR-04).
The salesperson shall enter a discount as a percentage (0 to 100, up to two decimals) on the pricing screen. The platform shows the discount amount and the net monthly price.
A discount up to and including the discount cap shall be applied without approval.
The cap shall be checked on the server. A request that applies a discount above the cap without an approval is refused, whatever the client sends.
An offer shall be created from the pricing screen of a deal (FR-PRC-12). Every offer belongs to exactly one deal and one company.
The salesperson may add a free-text note to the offer (e.g. special conditions). Prices cannot be edited on the offer; they come only from the pricing screen.
Each offer shall store the pricing inputs, the rule values used (snapshot) and the resulting amounts, so it can be re-displayed and re-downloaded identically later.
A price calculation shall return in under 300 ms and an offer PDF shall be generated in under 3 seconds on the staging server.

The offer shall be filled automatically with: offer number and date, validity date, Wellness Albania details (FR-PCF-08), company name, NIPT (if recorded), address with predefined Area and City, primary contact person with position (or the contact chosen), number of employees, business type, risk level, visit frequency, service package and its services, price breakdown, list price, discount % and amount, net monthly price, annual value, "VAT not included" note (Q5), standard texts, and the salesperson's name, phone and email.
The salesperson shall preview the offer in the browser as it will appear in the PDF.
The salesperson shall download the offer as a PDF named "Oferta_<company>_<number>.pdf" in Albanian or English (chosen when downloading; default = Albanian).
Offers shall not be sent by email from the platform in this milestone. The existing quotation email and public share link shall be disabled for the Wellness Albania workspace.
Offers shall be numbered sequentially per year with the configured prefix, e.g. OF-2026-0001. Numbers are never reused, including for deleted drafts.
Offer statuses: Draft, Pending approval, Ready, Sent, Accepted, Rejected, Expired. Only Ready offers can be downloaded as final; drafts download with a "DRAFT" watermark.
After emailing the PDF, the salesperson clicks "Mark as sent" and enters the date sent (default today). The validity date is counted from that date.
Changing a Sent offer shall create a new version (OF-2026-0001 v2) and keep the previous version read-only. Only the latest version can be accepted.
The salesperson shall mark an offer Accepted or Rejected (with an optional note). Accepting an offer is the normal way to win the deal (FR-DEAL-07).
A Sent offer past its validity date shall become Expired automatically (existing expiry job).
Users shall list offers with filters by status, salesperson, company and date, within their data scope.
Offer status changes and final prices shall be recorded in the offer history and the audit log.
The existing workspace-wide quotation approval switch and quotations.approve shall be replaced for the Wellness Albania workspace by the discount approval of section 5.
All new screens, messages, notifications, the offer PDF and the seeded lists shall be translated in sq and en.

A discount above the cap shall require approval. The salesperson must give a reason; the offer moves to "Pending approval" and cannot be downloaded as final, marked as sent or used to win the deal until approved.
When approval is requested, every user with "Discounts: approve" in scope shall receive an in-app notification, and an email if enabled in notification settings. The notification opens the request.
The approver shall see a list of pending approval requests and approve or reject each one with an optional comment (required when rejecting). The approver may approve a lower % than requested.
The salesperson shall be notified of the decision. Approved: the offer becomes ready to download. Rejected: the offer returns to draft with the discount set back to the cap, and the comment is shown.

An approval shall apply to that offer version, list price and discount only. If the inputs change so that the list price changes, or the discount is raised, a new approval is needed. Lowering the discount keeps the approval.
A user cannot approve their own request. A Sales Manager's own discount above the cap goes to the other users with "Discounts: approve" (by default the CEO, Q8).
The salesperson can withdraw a pending request.
Requests, approvals, rejections and withdrawals shall be written to the audit log with the requested %, approved %, list price and comment.
A pending request older than a configurable number of hours (default 24) shall remind the approver once.
After saving an activity, the user shall be offered the one-click follow-up buttons (FR-FUP-01) in the same dialog.
Deals with an overdue follow-up, or with no activity for a configurable number of days (default 14), shall be highlighted on the board and the list.

On the company page, the deal page and after saving an activity, the user shall schedule a follow-up with one click: one button per active follow-up interval from Milestone 1 (default 3, 5, 7 days) and a "Custom date" button.

A follow-up shall have: company, deal (optional), type of next contact (default Call), due date and time (default time 09:00, editable), assigned salesperson (default the deal's or company's), and a short note (default the activity's "next action").
Follow-up days shall be calendar days. If the due date falls on a Saturday or Sunday it moves to the next Monday (Q12).
A follow-up shall appear automatically in the assigned salesperson's calendar and in "My follow-ups".
A follow-up not completed by its due date and time shall be marked Overdue (shown in red) until it is completed, rescheduled or cancelled.

The user completes a follow-up by recording the activity that happened (FR-ACT-02); the follow-up is then closed and linked to that activity. The user can also reschedule it (new date, previous date kept in its history) or cancel it with a reason.
"My follow-ups" shall list the user's open follow-ups grouped as Overdue, Today, and Upcoming, with the count of overdue items also shown in the main menu.
The Sales Manager shall see the follow-ups of the whole team with a salesperson filter, and a list of all overdue follow-ups across the team. The CEO sees the same, read-only.
The assigned salesperson shall receive an in-app notification when a follow-up becomes due (at its due time), and an optional daily email summary of the day's follow-ups.
The Sales Manager can reassign a follow-up to another salesperson.

The salesperson calendar shall show, in day, week and month views and an agenda list: follow-ups (including calls to make), meetings, visits, online meetings and other planned activities, and overdue items. Each type has its own colour and icon.
The user shall plan a meeting, visit, online meeting or call from the calendar or from a company/deal, with company, deal, contact person, start and end time, place (for visits) and note.
Clicking a calendar item shall open a panel with its details and actions (complete, reschedule, cancel, open company, open deal).
Overdue items shall be shown on today's date in an "Overdue" section of the day and agenda views, not only on their original date.
The Sales Manager calendar shall show the items of all Sales Users, with a filter to show one, several or all salespeople and a colour per salesperson; overdue follow-ups are included.
The CEO shall see all calendars, read-only. The Administrator and Reception have no sales calendar unless granted (M1 matrix).
The user can reschedule an item by dragging it to another time on desktop.
The calendar shall respect the workspace time zone (Europe/Tirane) and the user's language for day and month names.

A deal shall be won from one of its ready, sent or accepted offers, recording the closing date, the agreed monthly price and annual value, the package and the salesperson. The agreed price is read from the offer and cannot be typed.
Winning a deal shall turn its company into a Client and, when the user confirms, close the deal's open follow-ups.
A deal shall be lost with a reason chosen from the predefined lost reasons and an optional note; its open offers become Rejected and its open follow-ups are closed.
A user with "Deals: reopen" shall reopen a won or lost deal into an open stage with a comment; the previous result is kept in the history.
Winning, losing, reopening and every change of the agreed values shall be recorded in the audit trail.

The permission catalogue shall activate "Payments: view", "Payments: update" and "Performance: view", and add "Contracts: suspend, cancel, reinstate" (contracts.terminate). The existing "Contracts: view validity" and "Contracts: manage" keep their meaning. The Administrator can assign all of them from the Milestone 1 roles screen.
The default roles shall receive the permissions in the matrix in 7.2 on upgrade, once, without changing what the Administrator already customised (the upgrade ledger of Milestone 2).

Contract commercial fields (price, annual value, discount, services, package, terms, document, deal, offer) and all payment fields shall be removed from API responses for users without "Commercial details: view" or "Payments: view" respectively (extends Milestone 1 FR-RBAC-06 and Milestone 2 FR-RBAC-17). Reception receives only number, status, validity, start and end date, company.
The audit log viewer shall offer filters for the new entity types: Contract and Payment (instalment).

Each contract shall get a sequential number, per year, for example CTR-2026-0001, using the same numbering mechanism as offers (Milestone 2 FR-OFR-08). The number prefix is an offer-style setting of the Administrator.
The Administrator shall set the reminder lead times, in days before the end date, as a list. Default 60, 30 and 7. Changes apply to contracts not yet reminded at that lead time.
The "expiring soon" window shall be set by the Administrator (default 30 days). A valid contract ending within it shows the Expiring soon badge and counts in the dashboard figures.

A daily job shall set an instalment to Overdue when its due date has passed (plus the grace days of the Administrator, default 0) and it is Invoice Issued, Payment Pending or Partially Paid. An instalment past its due date that is still Not Invoiced keeps that status and is flagged "Due, not invoiced". The job records the change as done by the system and running it twice changes nothing.

In Milestone 3 the following shall be audited with old and new values, using the Milestone 1 audit mechanism (FR-AUD-03): creation of a contract from a deal; every change of a contract field, status (with reason), renewal link and "not renewing" mark; signed document attached or replaced; every instalment action (generated, added, changed, removed, invoice recorded, receipt recorded, status change with comment); and the reminder, expiring-soon and payment settings.
A user with "Contracts: manage" shall create a contract from a Won deal, from the deal screen and from the company page. A Won deal can have one contract.
A contract cannot exist without a won deal. Contracts created before this milestone (without a deal) stay readable and are marked "Legacy: no deal".

The contract shall be filled from the won deal and its offer: company, deal, offer, responsible salesperson, package and its services, agreed monthly price and annual value, discount %, and the offer terms text. Start date defaults to the deal closing date; end date defaults to start date plus the contract months of the offer minus one day. Billing period defaults to monthly.

The agreed price, annual value, package and services shall be copied onto the contract and are read only. They cannot be typed. While the contract is Draft, a "Refresh from deal" action re-reads them from the deal (for example after the Sales Manager reopened the deal and a new offer was won). From Pending Signature on, they are locked.

The contract record shall show: number, status, validity, company, deal, offer, responsible salesperson, package and services, start date, end date, renewal date, agreed monthly price, annual value, discount %, billing period, commercial terms, notes, signed document, previous term (if a renewal), status history and the payment schedule summary.

The renewal date shall default to the end date minus the largest reminder lead time (FR-REN-01) and can be changed while the contract is Draft or Active. It is the date by which the renewal should be agreed.

The contract list shall search and filter by number, company, status, validity, responsible salesperson, end date range and payment state (any overdue instalment), and by predefined Area and City of the company. Results respect the scope of the user (Own, Team, All).
Contracts shall appear on the company page and in the company history timeline (Milestone 1 FR-CMP-05): created, status changes, document attached, renewed.

While a contract is Draft, the user can edit dates, billing period, commercial terms, renewal date, notes and responsible salesperson. After activation only notes, the signed document and the renewal date can be changed. A contract cannot be deleted; a Draft is cancelled instead.

Own, Team and All shall mean for contracts and payments what they mean for companies (Milestone 1 section 4.3): Own is the contracts and instalments of companies where the user is the responsible salesperson; Team is those of all Sales Users; All is everything. The Sales Manager never sees data of other roles or of companies outside the sales team (Dimitris).
The CEO shall be read only for contracts and payments. Only "Payments: update" changes payments, and a Sales User or Sales Manager never does, even for their own contracts.

Contract amounts, instalments, receipts, outstanding amounts and all money figures on dashboards and the performance screen shall be calculated as Decimal (two decimals, half-up), never Float. The existing Float columns of Contract and ContractPayment shall be converted (Milestone 2 D4).
One contract per won deal and one reminder per contract and lead time shall be guaranteed by the database (unique constraints), not only by the application.

Migrations shall run on PostgreSQL and MySQL, including the Float to Decimal conversion, the new default payment status, existing contracts without a deal (marked Legacy) and the replacement of the reminder marker, and be reversible or backed up.
The transitions above, and only these, shall be allowed, and enforced on the server for every request. Any other transition is refused with a clear message.

Validity shall be one rule, calculated on the server: a contract is valid when its status is Active and today is between its start and end date, both included. Every other contract is not valid, with the reason shown as its status (Pending Signature, Suspended, Expired, Cancelled, Draft) or "Not started".

Users with "Contracts: view validity" shall see a validity badge (Valid, Expiring soon, Not valid with reason) with start and end date in company search results, on the company page and on the contract list. They shall not see the price, services, commercial terms, discount, payments, deal, offer or document.
When a company has more than one contract, the badge shall reflect the contract valid today (the one ending last if several), otherwise the latest contract.

A daily job shall set an Active contract to Expired when its end date has passed, in the workspace time zone, record the change as done by the system, and notify the responsible salesperson and the Sales Manager if no renewal exists. Running the job twice shall change nothing the second time.

When the last valid or upcoming contract of a company has Expired or been Cancelled and no renewal deal is open, the company status shall change to Former client. A new activated contract sets it back to Client.

The scheduled jobs (expiry, renewal reminders, overdue instalments) shall be idempotent, use the workspace time zone, record "system" as the actor, and catch up after a missed run (for example after a restart) without duplicating anything.

When a contract is activated, the platform shall generate one instalment per billing period of the term, as the existing schedule does: the first instalment due on the start date and the next ones on the same day of each following period (clamped to the last day of a shorter month), none starting after the end date, at most 120. Each instalment gets the contract price for one period, as Decimal, status Not Invoiced and nothing received.
Each instalment shall record: due date, amount, status, amount received, date received, payment method (Bank transfer, Cash, Card, Other), invoice number, invoice date and a note.

An authorized user shall be able to add an extra instalment, change the due date or amount of an instalment that has nothing received, and remove an instalment that has nothing received, each with a reason. An instalment with any amount received cannot be removed. Changing the contract price later never changes instalments already issued (the existing rule).

Only users with "Payments: update" shall create, change or remove instalments, record invoices and record receipts. Sales User, Sales Manager, Reception and CEO cannot, even for their own contracts. The rule is enforced on the server.

The status of an instalment shall follow the table above: moving to Invoice Issued requires an invoice number and date; Payment Pending needs an invoice; Partially Paid and Paid are set by recording a receipt, never by choosing the status; Overdue is set by the system. An authorized user can correct an instalment back to an earlier status with a comment.

Recording a receipt shall require the amount, the date received (not in the future) and the method, and shall add the amount to the amount already received. A receipt that would exceed the instalment amount is refused. The status becomes Partially Paid or Paid automatically.
Every change to an instalment shall be written to its history with who (or "system"), when, old and new status, the amount received and a comment, and shown on the instalment.
The contract shall show a payment summary: total of instalments, received, outstanding, next due date and the number and amount overdue, calculated from its instalments.

Users with "Payments: view" shall see instalments read only, and users without "Commercial details: view" shall see no amounts (Reception sees no payment data at all). Payment fields are removed from API responses for users without the permission.
Marking a contract Pending Signature shall require start date, end date, billing period and price, and shall lock the commercial values (FR-CON-04).
Activating a contract shall require the signed document (FR-CON-19). Activation generates the payment schedule (FR-PAY-02) and sets the company status to Client (Milestone 1 Q9) if it is not already.
Suspending and reinstating a contract shall require a reason, which is stored on the status history and shown on the contract. A suspended contract is not valid (FR-CON-20).

Cancelling a contract shall require a reason. Future instalments that are still Not Invoiced are removed. Instalments already invoiced, partly paid or paid stay and must be settled or corrected by an authorized user.
Every status change shall be written to the contract status history with who (or "system"), when, the old and new status and the reason, and shown on the contract.

The signed contract document shall be attached to the contract as a PDF (maximum 15 MB, checked by content, not by file name). Replacing it keeps the earlier file as a previous version with date and user. Viewing and downloading requires "Commercial details: view" and access to the contract.

Winning a deal, creating a contract and activating a contract shall be separate from confirming payment: winning a deal never creates or changes an instalment, and no user can mark an instalment Paid because of a deal or contract status.

Contract status transitions, payment permissions, payment status rules, data scope, field removal and document access shall be enforced on the server for every request. The signed document is validated by content, size and type.

A Payments overview shall list instalments with filters by status, company, responsible salesperson, due date range, and contract, with totals of amount, received and outstanding for the filtered list. Scope follows the user: Sales User Own, Sales Manager Team, CEO and authorized payment users All.
When an instalment becomes Overdue, the authorized payment users, the responsible salesperson and the Sales Manager shall get a notification (once per instalment), so the client can be contacted.
The payments overview and a contract's instalments shall export to CSV for users who can view them. The export is recorded in the audit log.
Exports of payments and performance (FR-PAY-14, FR-PRF-09) shall be recorded in the audit log with who, when and the filters used. Viewing a dashboard is not audited.

"Start renewal" shall create a deal of type Renewal for the company, linked to the contract, owned by the responsible salesperson, in the stage Interested (editable), with the company data filled in. The salesperson then prices and offers it with the Milestone 2 flow.

When a Renewal deal is won, "Create contract" (FR-CON-01) shall pre-fill the start date as the day after the previous end date and link the new contract to the previous one (previous term and renewed into). The previous contract stays unchanged in its own status and history.
Contracts shall never renew automatically. A renewal always goes through a deal and an offer.

At each lead time a reminder shall go to the responsible salesperson and to every user with "Contracts: manage" at Team or All scope for that contract (by default the Sales Manager), in the app and by email if enabled in notification settings. The reminder opens the contract and offers "Start renewal".

A reminder for a contract and a lead time shall be sent once. The sent reminders shall be recorded per contract and lead time, and a failure to send is retried on the next run. A renewal contract starts with no reminders sent.

A Renewals screen shall list valid contracts ending in the next 30, 60 or 90 days, and contracts expired in the last 90 days, with end date, days remaining, responsible salesperson, monthly price and renewal state: Not started, In negotiation (an open renewal deal), Renewed, Not renewing. Scope follows the user (Own, Team, All).
The salesperson can mark a contract "Not renewing" with a reason from the predefined lost-deal reasons (Milestone 1 FR-SET-06) and a note. No further reminders are sent for it.
A contract that ended without a renewal shall stay visible in "Recently expired" for 90 days so the team can win the client back, and the company status follows FR-CON-17.
Contract end dates and renewal dates of the user's scope shall appear in the sales calendar as read-only items that open the contract.

Each dashboard and the performance screen shall load in under 2 seconds with 2,000 deals, 5,000 activities, 500 contracts and 6,000 instalments on the staging server. The contract and payment lists shall load in under 2 seconds with the same data.

Users with "Performance: view" shall open a Performance screen with one row per salesperson and a total row. Scope: Sales User Own (only their own row, no ranking and no other salesperson's figures), Sales Manager Team (all Sales Users), CEO All. The Administrator has no access by default.

The screen shall filter by salesperson (one or several, for Sales Manager and CEO) and by date range: presets (This week, This month, Last month, This quarter, This year) and a custom range. Default is This month.

For each salesperson the screen shall show: number of calls, emails, visits and meetings; companies contacted; offers created; offers sent; deals won; deals lost; total value of won deals; conversion rate; follow-ups completed; overdue follow-ups; and average time to close.
The total row shall be calculated from the underlying data of the selected salespeople, not by averaging the rows (conversion rate and average time to close in particular).

Each indicator shall be attributed to the date of its own event (date of contact, date offer was marked sent, won date, lost date, completion date) in the workspace time zone, and to the salesperson responsible for the record at that time. Salespeople deactivated later keep their history.
The user shall be able to compare with the previous period of the same length (each indicator shows the change).
Clicking an indicator of a row opens the underlying records (activities, offers, deals, follow-ups) with the same filters.
A salesperson detail view shall show the indicators per week or month as a chart with a table view.
The screen shall export the filtered table to PDF and CSV, using the existing report output. Exports are recorded in the audit log.
Value figures (offers value, total value, sales value) shall be hidden for any user without "Commercial details: view" and removed from the API response.
The dashboard and performance endpoints shall enforce the scope on the server (FR-DSH-02, FR-PRF-01), whatever filters the client sends.
Every figure in sections 5.3 and 6.2 shall be reproduced exactly on a fixed set of test data, including the conversion rate and sales value example in 5.3 and the total-row example in FR-PRF-04.

After login, each user shall land on the dashboard of their role: Sales User, Sales Manager, Administrator or CEO. Reception lands on the company search of Milestone 1 and has no dashboard. The dashboard is also reachable from the main menu.

Every number shall be calculated on the server within the data scope of the user: Sales User Own, Sales Manager Team (the sales team only), Administrator and CEO All. A user cannot obtain another scope by changing the request.

Dashboards shall have a period selector: Today, This week, This month (default), This quarter, This year and a custom range. Period figures (for example deals won) follow it. Figures that describe the situation now (open pipeline, active contracts) do not, and are labelled "as of now".
Dashboards that can be filtered by company location shall offer the predefined Area and City lists, never free text.

Each figure shall show its value, its label, and whether it follows the period or is as of now. Where a list sits behind it (for example overdue follow-ups, expiring contracts, overdue instalments), clicking it opens that list already filtered.

Money is shown in EUR with two decimals and the Albanian or English number format of the user. Charts have a table view with the same numbers. A dashboard with no data shows an empty state, not zeros without explanation.
The dashboard shall show the time it was calculated and a refresh button. Figures are calculated when the page is opened, not stored.

Figures that contain prices, offers, deal values, contract values or payments shall be hidden for any user without "Commercial details: view" (or "Payments: view" for payments), and removed from the API response.

Sales User dashboard. Own leads; own active deals with a count per stage; follow-ups due today and in the next 7 days; overdue follow-ups; offers created and offers sent in the period; deals won in the period; own sales value in the period; own activity in the period (calls, emails, visits, meetings). Should: own contracts expiring soon and own overdue instalments.

Sales Manager dashboard. Total leads and leads per salesperson; active deals; the full team pipeline (count and value per stage); offers created and sent; follow-ups due and overdue, in total and per salesperson; deals won and lost; conversion rate in total and per salesperson; total sales value and per salesperson; activity per salesperson; lost-deal analysis (count and value per lost reason). Should: pending discount approvals, contracts expiring soon and overdue instalments of the team.

Administrator dashboard. Pricing configuration summary (discount cap, active employee bands, risk surcharges, visit frequencies, price zones, and the date of the last change of each); current users per role and inactive users; recent changes from the audit log (the last 20, with a link to the full log); items needing attention (for example cities in no price zone, a role with no users). It shows no sales figures.

CEO dashboard. Total sales pipeline (count and value); sales value in the period; revenue in the period; monthly recurring value of active contracts; sales performance over time (per month); team performance (per salesperson table); contracts: active, expired and expiring soon, with count and value; payments: count and amount per payment status, outstanding and overdue; operational indicators: overdue follow-ups, pending discount approvals, offers waiting; company counts per status. A place for the Wellness+ indicators is prepared and stays empty until Milestone 4.
The CEO dashboard is read only. It can open any list behind a figure but not edit it (Milestone 1 Q7 default).
All Milestone 3 screens, including the dashboards, Renewals, Payments overview and Performance screen, shall work on desktop and mobile from 360 px wide.
All new screens, messages, notifications, status labels and chart labels shall be translated in sq and en.
The Milestone 3 requirement IDs shall be added to scripts/srs-requirements.json as each implementation slice starts, so the CI traceability check covers them.
Fees, discounts, upgrade differences, payments and revenue shall be calculated as Decimal (two decimals, half up), never Float.
Every figure in section 9.3 shall be reproduced exactly on a fixed set of test data, including the worked example.

Validity shall be one rule, calculated on the server: a member is valid when the status is Active. Every Active member is valid at least as Bronze. Every other member is not valid, with the status as the reason. The tier is never a reason for not being valid.

The effective tier of a member shall be the highest tier among the terms valid today, with Bronze as the floor. A sponsored term counts only while the employer has a valid contract (Milestone 3 FR-CON-20); a term counts until its end date plus the grace days (FR-TIR-05). It is one rule in the domain, used by the list, the card, Reception, partner verification and the reports.

A paid term shall start on the payment date for a new purchase, an upgrade or a purchase after the previous term ended, and on the day after the current end date for a renewal. It ends on the start date plus the term months minus one day.
A renewal can be recorded at any time while a paid term is valid or within the grace days after it ended. A payment for the same tier after that is a new purchase and starts on the payment date.
The Administrator shall set the grace days (default 0). The member keeps the tier during the grace days, and the daily job downgrades only after term end plus grace days.

When a paid term has ended without renewal, the member shall be downgraded one step: Gold to Silver, Silver to Bronze. The Silver term created by a Gold downgrade lasts 12 months from the next day and, if not renewed, ends in Bronze in the same way.

The Administrator shall set the "expiring soon" window (default 30 days). A paid term ending within it shows the Expiring soon badge, counts in the reports and appears in the list of expiring memberships (FR-RPT-09).

The amount shall be calculated on the server by the price rule above from the fee settings and the family discount valid on the payment date. Silver and Gold can be bought by any Active member. VIP cannot be bought.

Any Active member, including a family member and a sponsored Silver employee, can upgrade to a higher paid tier by paying the difference. A payment cannot move a member to a lower tier. Bronze to Gold is allowed in one step at the full Gold price.

An upgrade shall start the new term on the payment date for the full term length and close the member's earlier paid term the day before. A sponsored term is left as it is. A member has at most one paid term at a time.

The family discount (Administrator setting, default 50%) shall apply to the price of Silver and Gold, to renewals and to upgrades of a family member, on the payment date, when the principal is Active and has the effective tier Silver, Gold or VIP. Otherwise the full price applies.
An approval shall create a VIP term from the approval date for the VIP term length (default 12 months), free of charge, with the review date equal to its end date. No payment is created.

The approvers shall be notified once, 30 days before the review date, and the member list shall offer the filter "VIP review due". A new approved request before the end extends VIP from the next day. If the VIP term ends without a new approval, the member falls back to the highest other valid tier, Bronze if none.

Sponsored Silver shall last as long as the employer company has a valid contract. The expiry date shown on the member is the end date of that contract. When a renewal contract takes over without a gap, the employees stay Silver and their expiry date moves to the new end date, with no action by anyone.

The permission catalogue shall get a Wellness+ group with these permissions: Members: view; Members: verify; Members: manage; Members: view payments; Members: record payments; Members: import employees; Members: approve VIP; Members: view reports; Wellness+ settings: manage. The Administrator can assign all of them from the Milestone 1 roles screen.
The default roles shall receive the permissions in the matrix in 10.2 on upgrade, once, without changing what the Administrator already customised (the upgrade ledger, Milestone 2 D7).

Fields shall be removed from API responses, not only hidden: payment fields for users without "Members: view payments"; phone, email, internal note and verification log for users with only "Members: verify"; every Wellness+ field for users without any Wellness+ permission. Reception receives only the fields in FR-VER-02.

Members belong to the workspace, not to a salesperson: there is no Own or Team scope for members. A user holding a Wellness+ permission sees all members; a user without it sees none and gets 403 on direct calls.
The CEO shall be read only for Wellness+: by default "Members: view", "Members: view payments" and "Members: view reports", and no write permission (as Milestone 1 Q7, Milestone 3 FR-RBAC-24).
The card page and the public verification page are the only endpoints without login. Every other Wellness+ endpoint shall check the permission on the server for every request.
The audit log viewer shall offer filters for the new entity types: Member, Membership payment and Wellness+ settings.

A user whose role holds Wellness+ permissions shall reach membership and commercial information only: members, payments, reports, and the company and contract validity data that Reception already sees. A Membership Agent role needs no commercial details of contracts (price, terms, document).

Tier rules, permissions, field removal, the card and verification rules and the import limits shall be enforced on the server for every request. Card tokens shall come from a cryptographically secure generator, be unique in the database and be at least 128 bits.

Each member shall get a unique member ID made of a prefix and a six-digit sequential number, for example WP-000123, using the same numbering mechanism as offers and contracts but without a yearly restart. The prefix is a setting of the Administrator. An ID is never changed or reused, even after the member is closed.

The Administrator shall set the labels (Albanian and English) and colour of the four tiers, the fee and term length in months of Silver and Gold (defaults €60 and €100, 12 months) and the term length of VIP (default 12 months). Bronze and VIP are free and cannot be given a fee. A new fee applies to payments recorded after the change; recorded payments never change.

Each payment shall get a sequential receipt number per year, for example RCP-2027-000045, using the same numbering mechanism as offers (Milestone 2 FR-OFR-08). The receipt is a record, not a legal invoice. The Administrator can set the prefix.

The Administrator shall manage the relationship list (Albanian and English labels, order, active or not). The seed list is Spouse or partner, Child and Parent, as in the strategy. A deactivated relationship is not offered for new links and stays on existing ones.

The Administrator shall manage the list of services (Albanian and English name, order, active or not) and, for each service and each tier (Bronze, Silver, Gold, VIP), a discount percentage from 0 to 100 with up to two decimals. An empty value means no discount.
A new installation shall be seeded with the table in 6.1, with VIP equal to Gold, so the module is usable before Wellness Albania sends its final numbers. Every value is editable.
All users with "Members: view" or "Members: verify" can open the benefit table read only, with the tiers as columns.
A change in the table shall apply at once to the card and the verification screen and is audited with the old and new value. There is no per-member exception and no history of past tables.
The platform shows the discount that applies. It does not apply the discount to bills or bookings and does not record which services a member used (out of scope, section 1.2).

In Milestone 4 the following shall be audited with old and new values, using the Milestone 1 audit mechanism: creation and every change of a member, status change with reason, tier correction, payment recorded or voided, VIP request, decision and ending, family link, confirmation and removal, employee upload (company, counts, file name), removal from a company, card link replaced, anonymisation or export of a member, and every change of the settings (fees, terms, grace days, expiring-soon window, numbering prefixes, relationship list, benefit services and percentages).

All Milestone 4 staff screens, messages, notifications and tier and benefit labels shall be translated in Albanian and English. The card and the public verification page shall be in Albanian and English; Greek and Italian are Should.
Migrations shall run on PostgreSQL and MySQL, add the new permissions through the upgrade ledger, seed the tier settings, the relationship list and the benefit table, and be reversible or backed up.

Card links and QR codes shall be built from one configured public base URL. The production address is fixed before the first card is issued; if it ever changes, the old address redirects to the new one so issued cards keep working.

A user with "Members: manage" shall register a member by hand. First name and last name are required, and at least one of date of birth, phone or email, so the person can be recognised later. A new member is Bronze, Active, with the start date today.

The member record shall hold: member ID, first name, last name, date of birth, phone, email, card language (Albanian by default; English, Greek, Italian), city (from the predefined Area and City lists, optional), tier, status, start date, expiry date, employer company, family link, internal note, created by and when. It holds no medical information (FR-DPR-01).

The platform shall prevent a second record for the same person: a member with the same email, or the same phone, or the same first name, last name and date of birth, is reported before saving. The agent can confirm "different person" and save. Imports (FR-EMP-04) report such rows and never create them.

A member has the status Active, Suspended or Closed. A user with "Members: manage" can suspend a member with a reason (card not valid, no discounts, tier unchanged) and reinstate. Closing keeps the record and the ID for history; a closed member can be reopened. No member is deleted.

The member list shall search by name, member ID, phone and email and filter by tier, status, validity, source (corporate, individual, family), employer company, expiring soon, VIP review due and former employee, plus the Area and City of the employer company from the predefined lists. It pages and sorts.

The member page shall show all fields, the current tier with its term dates, the term history, the tier history, payments (for users who may see them, FR-MPAY-08), the family group, the employer company, the verification events (FR-VER-06) and the internal note.

Personal details (name, date of birth, phone, email, language, city, note) can be edited by users with "Members: manage". The tier, the term dates, the status history and the member ID cannot be typed: they change only through the actions in this milestone (payment, upgrade, VIP, import, removal, correction).
The member page shall let an authorized user write an internal note. The note field shows a warning that no medical information may be written there.

Every change of effective tier shall be written to the tier history with the date, the old and new tier, the reason (Purchase, Renewal, Upgrade, Not renewed, Company contract ended, Left company, VIP approved, VIP ended, Import, Correction), who (or "system") and a comment.

The platform shall hold no medical information about members: no diagnosis, no result, no service used, no medical note. The member fields are those in FR-MEM-02 and nothing in the member record, the card or the reports is derived from medical data.
The platform shall collect the minimum: no national identity number, address, photograph or health data. Date of birth is optional and used for identification at Reception.

The database shall guarantee: one member number and one card token per value; one receipt number per value; one open VIP request per member; one employer per member; one principal per family member; one discount per service and tier.

The member list and search shall return in under 1 second with 50,000 members; Reception verification and the public verification page in under 1 second; the card page shall be usable in under 2 seconds on a mid-range phone on 4G; the preview of a 1,000-row upload in under 15 seconds and its confirmation in under 30 seconds; the reports and the dashboard block in under 2 seconds with 50,000 members and 20,000 payments.

Only users with "Members: record payments" shall record a membership payment. The user chooses the member, the kind (New, Renewal, Upgrade), the target tier, the method (Cash, Bank transfer, Card, Other) and the date received (not in the future) and may add a note. The amount is calculated by the platform and shown; it cannot be typed.

A user with "Members: record payments" shall be able to void the latest payment of a member with a required reason. Voiding reverses its effect (the earlier tier and term are restored), keeps the receipt number marked Voided and is written to the history. An earlier payment cannot be voided while a later one exists.

A Membership payments list shall show payments with filters by date range, tier, kind, method, agent and status (Recorded or Voided), with totals of the filtered list that exclude voided payments. It is open to users with "Members: view payments".
Users without "Members: view payments" shall see no fee, amount, receipt or revenue field. These fields are removed from API responses, not only hidden. Reception sees tier and validity only.
A sponsored Silver membership shall not create a payment: the company pays under its contract. No fee is recorded for the employee.

Each payment shall store the list fee, the family discount percentage and the amount, so a later change of fee or discount never changes it. The list of payments and one member's payments can be exported to CSV by users who can view them; the export is audited.

A printable receipt (PDF) with the Wellness+ logo, member name and ID, tier, period, amount, method, receipt number and the agent shall be available from the payment, stating that it is not an invoice.

Exports (FR-RPT-10, FR-MPAY-10), the card links sheet (FR-EMP-08) and card link replacement shall be recorded with who, when and the filters used, never with a token. Verifications are kept in their own log (FR-VER-06, FR-VER-10), not in the audit log. Viewing a report or dashboard is not audited.

A user with "Members: manage" shall add a family member to a principal member, by creating a new member or linking an existing one. The user must choose the relationship from the relationship list and tick that the relationship was confirmed. The platform stores who confirmed it and when.
A family member is a full member with an own ID, card, tier and terms. A family member has one principal; a principal cannot be a family member of another; nobody is linked to themselves.
The payment screen shall show the list fee, the discount and the reason "Family discount, relationship (name)", and the payment shall store them.
A user with "Members: manage" can remove a family link with a reason. The family member keeps the membership and all terms; later payments are at the full price. The change is recorded.
The principal's page shall list the family group with relationship, tier and validity, and each member's page shall show the principal. All links, confirmations and removals are audited.
Sponsored Silver covers the employee only. A family member of an employee does not get a sponsored term; the family discount applies when the employee is Silver or higher (FR-FAM-04).
A user with "Members: manage" shall request VIP for a member with a required reason (for example strategic client, PR relationship, key partner). The request has the status Pending.
Only a user with "Members: approve VIP" shall approve or reject a request, and a rejection needs a reason. A user cannot approve a request they made themselves.
A user with "Members: approve VIP" can end a VIP early with a reason. Requests, decisions and endings are shown on the member page and audited.

A daily job shall record the changes in FR-TIR-06, in FR-EMP-10 and in FR-VIP-04: new terms, the tier history and a notification to the agents, in the workspace time zone, with "system" as the actor. Running it twice shall change nothing the second time, and after a missed run it shall catch up without duplicating anything.

A user with "Wellness+ settings: manage" shall be able to correct the tier of a member with a required reason and an end date. The correction is a term of its own, recorded in the history with the reason Correction.

Once per member and term, the users who can record payments shall get a notification when the term enters the expiring soon window, so the member can be contacted. A daily summary instead of one message per member is acceptable.
The daily member job shall be idempotent, use the workspace time zone, record "system" as the actor and catch up after a missed run without duplicating any term, history entry or notification.

A user with "Members: import employees" shall upload an employee list for one company, from the Wellness+ tab of the company page and from the Wellness+ menu. The company must have a valid contract today (Milestone 3 FR-CON-20); otherwise the upload is refused with the reason.

The platform shall offer a template to download with the columns First name*, Last name*, Date of birth, Phone, Email and Language (sq, en, el, it; empty means sq). Column names in Albanian and English are accepted. Each row needs a first name, a last name and at least one of date of birth, phone or email.

The file shall be checked by content, not by name: an Excel .xlsx workbook, at most 2 MB and 1,000 data rows (the limits of the existing client import), first sheet only, blank rows ignored. Macro files are refused. Cell values are read as text; formulas are never evaluated by the platform.

Before anything is created the platform shall show a preview that classifies each row: New member; Existing member to link (found by FR-MEM-04 and not linked to another company); Already linked to this company, or repeated in the file (skipped); Linked to another company (refused); Error (with the reason). It shows the counts. Nothing is created until the user confirms.

On confirmation the platform shall create each new member with a unique member ID, the employer company, the language and a sponsored Silver term starting today, and link each existing member with a sponsored Silver term. Everything of one upload is created in one transaction: if anything fails, nothing is created. The tier history records the reason Import.

After an upload the platform shall show the result (created, linked, skipped, errors) and offer an Excel file of the skipped and error rows with the row number and the reason. The upload is recorded with who, when, file name and counts, and listed on the Wellness+ tab of the company.
Uploading the same file again shall create nothing new: every row is reported as Already linked.
A member can be linked to one employer company at a time. Linking a second company is refused until the first link is removed.
Uploads shall be limited to .xlsx workbooks of at most 2 MB and 1,000 rows, checked by content; formulas and external links are never followed; exports protect against formula injection.

When the employer has no valid contract (Expired, Cancelled, Suspended or not started), the sponsored term shall not count, so the employee is Bronze unless a paid or VIP term gives a higher tier. The daily job records the change with the reason "Company contract ended" and the effect is also visible at once, because the effective tier is calculated (FR-TIR-02).

While an employee is still linked to the company, a new valid contract of the company, also after a gap, shall make the employee Silver again. A suspended contract makes the employees Bronze while it is suspended and Silver again when it is reinstated.

A user with "Members: manage" shall remove an employee from the company, with the leaving date (default today) and an optional reason. The employer link is cleared, the sponsored term ends and the effective tier becomes the highest own term, Bronze if none. The member is kept and listed as a former employee of that company, so the agent can contact the person and offer a paid membership. The tier history records "Left company".
The member list and the Wellness+ tab of the company shall have the filter "Former employees", with the company and the leaving date.
An agent shall be able to remove several selected employees at once, for example when a company reduces its staff.

The company page shall get a Wellness+ tab for users with "Members: view": the members linked to the company with the count per tier, the former employees, the upload button (FR-EMP-01) and the history of uploads. It shows "N members of M employees" where M is the employee count of the company record.

Each member shall have a personal card page at a private link that contains a random token of at least 128 bits and opens without login. The page shows the Wellness+ logo, name, member ID, tier (in its colour), validity ("Valid until dd.mm.yyyy", or "No expiry" for Bronze), the QR code and the benefits of the tier (FR-BEN-03). It shows no phone, email, date of birth, employer or payment.

The QR code shall contain the verification link of the member (FR-VER-08), not the plain member ID. It shall be at least 220 px wide, black on white with a quiet zone and error correction level M or higher, and shall be readable by the built-in camera of an iPhone and of an Android phone.

The card shall always show the situation at the time it is opened: tier, validity and benefits come from the server. For a suspended or closed member the card shows "Membership not valid, contact Wellness Albania" and no QR code.
The card shall be shown in the language of the member (Albanian by default) with a switch between Albanian and English. Greek and Italian are shown for members who have them.

The card and verification pages shall give the same neutral "Card not found" page for an unknown, replaced or malformed token, shall carry noindex, shall be rate-limited per IP, shall not put the token in server logs or audit entries and shall contain no analytics or third-party scripts.
A user with "Members: manage" shall be able to show the card QR on screen, copy the card link and print the card (credit card size and A6) from the member page.

A user with "Members: manage" shall be able to replace the card link of a member, for example when a phone is lost or the card was shared. The old link and every home-screen copy of it stop working at once and show "This card was replaced. Ask Wellness Albania for the new link." The replacement is audited.
The card page shall carry a short privacy line (who holds the data, why, whom to contact) in Albanian and English. The text comes from Wellness Albania.

The discounts of the effective tier of the member shall be shown on the verification screen (FR-VER-02) and, as "Your benefits", on the card page (FR-CRD-01). A suspended or closed member is shown no discounts.

The platform shall send nothing to the employees automatically. A user with "Members: manage" can download, for one upload, an Excel sheet with name and card link of each member, so the company or Wellness Albania can distribute the cards (Q14). The download is audited.

The card page and the public verification page shall be rate-limited per IP: by default 60 requests per hour for the card page and 300 per hour for verification, so a clinic scanning many members from one network is not blocked. The limits are settings.
The QR code shall stay scannable in dark mode and at low screen brightness: the card page always shows the code on a white square with a quiet zone.

A user with "Members: verify" shall find a member by scanning the QR code with the camera of the device in the browser, or by searching member ID, name, phone or email. The "Verify member" screen is in the main menu and works on a phone, a tablet and a desktop with a webcam.

The result shall show, large, Valid or Not valid; the name, member ID, tier, valid until, status and date of birth (for the identity check); and the discounts of the tier. For a suspended or closed member it shows Not valid with the status and no discounts. It shows no payment, fee, phone, email or employer.

Reception shall confirm the identity by comparing the name and date of birth with the person's identity document and press "Identity confirmed" or "Does not match". The choice is stored with the verification.
A scanned code that is unknown or replaced shall show "Member not found" with no other information.
The result shall always come from the server at that moment; nothing is cached on the device.
Every verification at Reception shall be recorded with the member, the user, the time, scan or search, the result and the identity choice, and shown on the member page for users with "Members: view".

A partner clinic shall scan the QR code with an ordinary phone camera. The link opens a public verification page, without login, that shows Valid or Not valid and, for a valid member, the full name, the member ID, the tier and the valid-until date. It shows no date of birth, contact details, employer, payment or discounts.

The QR code shall carry one link per member. The same link opened by a logged-in user with "Members: verify" shall show the Reception screen of FR-VER-02, and opened by anyone else the public page of FR-VER-07.

The public page shall give the same neutral answer for every reason a member is not valid (Not valid), and the same "Member not found" for an unknown token, so nothing is learned about suspended or closed members.
Each public verification shall be recorded with the time, the result and a hashed IP address, without identifying the clinic. Whether partner clinics must be registered and identified is open (Q15).

All Milestone 4 staff screens shall work on desktop and on mobile from 360 px wide, and the card, the QR scan and the add-to-home-screen steps shall be tested on a real iPhone (Safari) and a real Android phone (Chrome).

A Wellness+ reports page shall be open to users with "Members: view reports". It has the period selector of Milestone 3 (FR-DSH-03: Today, This week, This month (default), This quarter, This year, custom) and the filters tier, segment (corporate, individual), employer company and the predefined Area and City of the employer company. Every figure is calculated on the server.
The report shall show the active members per tier, with count and share, as of now, and the active members at the end of each month of the period per tier.
The report shall show the new members in the period, split by corporate and individual, and the new paid memberships (payments of kind New).
The report shall show the renewals: terms that ended in the period, how many were renewed and how many not, and the renewal rate, in total and per tier.
The report shall show the upgrades in the period: count and amount per path (Bronze to Silver, Bronze to Gold, Silver to Gold).
The report shall show the downgrades in the period: count per path (Gold to Silver, Silver to Bronze, VIP to lower) and per reason (Not renewed, Company contract ended, Left company, VIP ended).

The report shall compare corporate and individual members (count and share of the active members) and list, per employer company, the members, the sponsored Silver, the members who upgraded to a paid tier and the former employees, with a link to the company.
For users who can view payments, the report shall show the membership revenue in the period: money received per tier and per kind, excluding voided payments.
The report page shall offer working lists: memberships expiring in the window, VIP reviews due, and former employees to contact, each with the member, the date and a link to the member.

Every report shall have a table view and a CSV export. Exports are audited, cells that begin with =, +, - or @ are protected against formula injection, and an export contains contact details only for users with "Members: view".
